title: Team credential safelist experiments and wireframes
content:
Context:
Working doc for experiments around introducing a "credential safelist" model in the Org/Team settings console. Goal: make it explicit which API keys and service accounts are allowed to be used by inbound routes, CI systems, and 3rd-party integrations. Unblocks: safer defaults for orgs that want to restrict keys, easier audits, and a more forgiving rotation story for customers.

Audience:
- Product PMs (console)
- Eng/Platform implementing enforcement hooks (routing + auth)
- Security/Compliance reviewers
- Solutions/SEs for enterprise rollout guidance

High-level problem statements (observed in support + audits):
- Customers accidentally expose long-lived API keys on public repos; rotating is painful because many assets implicitly rely on keys (cron jobs, services).
- Service accounts are used for both CI and interactive tasks; hard to reason about scope and allowed consumers.
- Audit logs are noisy: distinguishing legitimate bulk rotations vs anomalous key usage is manual and error-prone.

Proposed product behaviors (experiments):
1) Safelist: a per-team allowlist of consumer identities (hostnames, service-account IDs, job IDs, IP CIDRs) that a credential may be associated with.
   - Credential view shows: last used by X, allowed consumers (safelist), effective policies, and enforcement mode (monitoring/enforce).
2) Enforcement modes:
   - Monitor-only: allow all usage but surface violations in audit / alerts (good for initial rollout).
   - Enforce: block token usage from consumers not on safelist (fail fast).
3) Scoped rotation: when rotating a key, UI shows impacted consumers (based on recent usage + safelist membership) with a checklist and rollback plan.
4) Bulk operations: bulk rotate + notify consumers + staged cutover using canary tokens.

Wireframe notes (quick ASCII sketches to capture layout ideas):
[Credential list - Team > Credentials tab]
---------------------------------------------------------------
| Search | Filters: type(API key | SA) | Enforcement: monitor/enforce |
---------------------------------------------------------------
| Name | Type | Last used | Safelist summary | Policy | Actions |
| my-service-key | API | 2024-10-11 | 3 consumers | monitor | rotate/disable |
| ci-deploy | SA  | 2024-09-30 | ALL 10 jobs | enforce  | rotate/impersonate |
---------------------------------------------------------------

[Credential detail panel]
---------------------------------------------------------------
| BACK | my-service-key (API)                                 [DISABLE] |
| Status: active  | Enforcement: monitor-only  | Scope: team-wide           |
| Created: 2023-12-01 | Last used: 2024-10-11 (api.redwood.app)            |
| Description: CI deploy key for batch imports                         |
---------------------------------------------------------------
| SAFELIST (allowed consumers)                 | USAGE HISTORY (timeline)  | IMPACT
| - ci-warehouse-job-12 (last seen 10/11)      | 10/01: read  | (estimated 8 consumers will fail on rotate)
| - deploy-runner-03 (last seen 09/30)         | 09/30: write | 2 external integrations (notify)
| - 52.12.0.0/24 (CIDR)                        | 08/02: read  | Suggested migration steps: notify teams, create canary token
---------------------------------------------------------------
| ENFORCEMENT MODE: [ Monitor ] [ Enforce ]  [ Save ]  [ Start rotation ] |

Behavioral details and decisions to capture:
- Safelist canonical identities: prefer stable service-account resource ids and job ids over ephemeral hostnames. Support CIDR patterns and OAuth client IDs.
- Discovery heuristics: use recent last-used data (30/90/365 windows) plus attribution data (user agent, IP) to suggest safelist members.
- UI suggestion: show confidence level for each suggested consumer (high/medium/low) and an origin link to the evidence (audit line id).
- Rollout approach: default to monitor-only for existing orgs, opt-in enforce for new orgs with 'strict-credential-control' toggle.

Audit view additions (quick notes):
- Pivot the audit log by credential ID, consumer identity, or impacted route.
- Add a "safelist violation" event type. Events include: violation_detected, violation_blocked, rotation_started, rotation_completed, safelist_updated.
- Event detail shows: evidence (IP/UA), enforcement-mode at time of event, suggested remediation.

Backlog grooming (epics / slices):
- CONSOLE-314: Safelist data model + enforcement API (backend) [blocked by auth-router work]
- CONSOLE-329: Credential detail ui + suggest/safelist edit flow (frontend)
- CONSOLE-332: Audit pivot + alerting on monitor->enforce transition
- CONSOLE-345: Bulk-rotate orchestration with canary tokens and notifications
- CONSOLE-360: Admin onboarding checklist + migration tool for teams with many legacy keys

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Team credentials list with enforcement toggle per credential (monitor vs enforce) and visible safelist summary.
- Credential detail shows suggested safelist members with evidence links and confidence.
- Audit log has new "safelist violation" event and can filter on credential+violation.
- Backend enforcement API accepts safelist and enforcement mode and returns deterministic allow/deny for sample consumer identities.

Open questions / risks (tickets / decisions):
- How to handle third-party integrations that authenticate via API key but change UA/IP frequently? (Possible: add oauth-client-id style tokens or require integration registration).
- Performance: real-time enforcement for high-throughput routes—need fast lookup (in-memory cache + hashed keys) vs eventual consistency.
- UX: accept that initial discover suggestions will have false positives; how to prevent accidental lockouts? Use dry-run and staged enforcement.
- Legal / compliance: storing evidence for suggestions may include IPs and UAs—confirm retention policy with Security.

Edge cases to prototype in usability tests:
- Rotating a key used by >100 consumers (bulk notify flow, staging cutover).
- Credential with no recent uses but present in safelist (how to surface stale entries).
- Mixed-enforcement across team (some credentials enforce, some not) and cross-team service accounts.

Next steps / immediate TODOs (owner tags):
- @Liam: spike on backend data model + API for safelist enforcement (due 2024-10-09) (linked CONSOLE-314).
- @Priya: low-fidelity clickthrough of credential detail + rotation flow for next design review (2024-10-11).
- @Omar: audit pipeline change - add new event types and sample alerts (2024-10-15).
- Product sync: schedule short demo for Security and SRE to validate enforcement perf expectations (invite: sec, sre, infra).

Notes to self / rough language for help text (short):
- Safelist = the set of identities that are allowed to use this credential. Use monitor mode first to see which consumers are actually using this key before switching to enforce.
- When rotating: create a canary token, update a single consumer, verify, then roll out wider. The console will estimate reachable consumers and send notifications if enabled.

Appendix: quick list of suggested microcopy lines
- Credential list row badge: "Enforce: will block unknown consumers"
- Safelist suggestion tooltip: "Suggested because this identity used this key X times in the last 30 days (evidence)"
- Rotation modal CTA: "Create canary + rotate (safe)" or "Rotate now (force)"

End of notes.

(Working doc, iterative — expect many small changes; will extract final PRD and handoff once spike outcomes are available.)
